rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites call Muhammad’s Companions foolish and say this privately; before believers they profess faith, then tell their chiefs they remain with them and only pretend to believe.
rows.anchor: هم أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When alone with their leaders, they profess loyalty to their religion and say their public profession is mockery, displaying what they do not inwardly believe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repays their mockery, gives them respite and long lives, and lets them wander perplexed in excessive disbelief.
rows.anchor: في إسرافهم ومجاوزتهم القدر في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They chose error and abandoned guidance; their trade did not profit them. Attributing profit to the trade is expansive usage, like attributing illumination to fire, and they were not guided.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant is God’s command in earlier scriptures to believe in Muhammad, confirmed as obligatory; cutting what should be joined means Quraysh’s hostile rupture of kinship with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وصيته وأمره في الكتب المتقدمة بالإيمان بمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They corrupt the earth through sins and by obstructing people from believing in Muhammad; they lose reward and incur punishment.
rows.anchor: بالـمعاصي وتعويق الناس عن الإيمان بمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How” is an astonished question directed to disbelievers for believers to marvel at: God gave life to those once dust, will kill them in this world, resurrect them, and judge them as He wills.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since polytheists deemed resurrection extraordinary, God argued with them from His creation of the heavens and earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is told to devote his religion sincerely to God in monotheism; alternatively, he is told to surrender himself. He answers with heart, tongue, and limbs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Jacob enjoined the religious way, or the word of sincerity, on their sons: Islam, the upright religion chosen by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not die except as Muslims” means adhere to Islam so death finds you still following it.
rows.anchor: الزموا الإسلام حتى إذا أدرككم الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse turns back to the Jews: “Were you witnesses?” means “Rather, were you present?” when Jacob was dying.
rows.anchor: ترك الكلام الأول، وعاد إلى مخاطبة اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews claimed Jacob advised his sons to follow Judaism; God refutes them because they were not present at his deathbed testament asking whom they would worship after him.
rows.anchor: فأكذبهم الله تعالى، وقال: أكنتم حاضرين وصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier community means Abraham, his sons, Jacob, and his sons; they have their deeds and you have yours, since each is accountable for its own works.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Medina’s Jews and Najran’s Christians, each of whom urged believers to adopt its religion as the only true one; the answer is to follow Abraham’s upright way toward Islam.
rows.anchor: نزلت في يهود المدينة ونصارى نجران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those concealing scripture are Jewish leaders who take bribes for hiding its revealed description of Muhammad; what they consume ends in fire, and God will neither address nor purify them favorably.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment by rejecting Muhammad’s message and concealing his description.
rows.anchor: حين جحدوا أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وكتموا نعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How patient they are with fire” asks what drove them to it by abandoning truth for falsehood; it is a rebuke.
rows.anchor: أي: فأي شيء صبرهم على النار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reading is “How audacious they are toward the Fire!”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they faced Goliath’s army, they prayed for patience to be poured on them and for their feet to be strengthened by strengthening their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God’s decree the Israelites routed their enemy; David, a prophet in their army, killed Goliath. God gave David Israel’s kingdom and kingship with prophethood, and taught armor-making and the language of birds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God’s restraint through Muslim armies, polytheists would dominate the earth, kill believers, and destroy lands and mosques.
rows.anchor: لولا دفع الله بجنود المسلمين لغلب المشركون على الأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrated signs are signs of God’s oneness, and Muhammad is one of the messengers whose signs have been recounted.
rows.anchor: هذه الآيات التي أخبرتك بها آيات الله، أي: علامات توحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return-to-God day is Judgment Day; each person receives the recompense of their deeds without any shortfall.
rows.anchor: يعني: يوم القيامة تردون فيه إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prohibiting usury, God permits forward-credit sales and commands writing and witnessing deferred debts to protect property; the trust exception in 2:283 abrogates this command.
rows.anchor: فلما حرم الله تعالى الربا أباح السلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A just scribe writes without altering amount or term and must not refuse when asked; this was first obligatory for writer and witness, then abrogated by the prohibition on harming them.
rows.anchor: بالحق والإنصاف، ولا يزيد في المال والأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As God taught him” recognizes God’s favor of literacy; the debtor dictates because he is liable and must acknowledge the debt aloud without reducing it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child, incapacitated fool, mute, or speech-impaired debtor has a guardian—an heir or representative—dictate truthfully on his behalf.
rows.anchor: { أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses are two free adult men of the believers, acceptable for their merit and religion; if one woman forgets, the other reminds her of the testimony.
rows.anchor: أي: من أهل ملتكم من الأحرار البالغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses must not refuse when summoned to bear or give testimony; parties should not let irritation keep them from recording a small or large debt through its due date.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is fairest before God, makes testimony more reliable because the record reminds witnesses, and best prevents doubt about amount or due date.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An immediate exchange of goods is exempt from writing because the risks of delayed payment are absent; witnessing spot sales is also no longer obligatory under the abrogated ruling.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن ما يخاف في النساء والتأجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on harming a scribe or witness forbids altering records, false testimony, and refusing to testify; doing so is sinful.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يزيد الكاتب أو ينقص أو يحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When traveling without a scribe, take a received pledge as security; if parties trust one another, the entrusted debtor must repay and fear God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not conceal testimony when called to give it; whoever conceals it is sinful in heart.
rows.anchor: { ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم } فاجر { قلبه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the accountability verse descended, Companions told the Prophet involuntary thoughts seemed beyond their control; he urged them to answer as Israel had not, “we hear and obey,” and God relieved them by saying no soul is burdened beyond its capacity, abrogating the earlier verse.
rows.anchor: جاء ناس من الصحابة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: كلفنا من العمل ما لا نطيق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative view restricts this to concealing or giving testimony; “God will call you to account” means He will inform you and make the matter known.
rows.anchor: إن هذا في كتمان الشهادة وإقامتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ earnings and profits are brief and perishing; “provision” is what is prepared for a guest and here means recompense and reward.
rows.anchor: أي: ذلك الكسب والربح متاع قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God has for the righteous is better than what disbelievers enjoy; the following passage mentions believing People of the Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must remain firm in their religion through hardship, or specifically in jihad; they must outlast their enemy and stay stationed in jihad through war and argument.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fools” means women and children; household wealth is a means of livelihood and worldly well-being. Guardians should retain and manage it, provide food and clothes, and speak kindly to dependents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Test orphans’ minds and religion until puberty; when they show sound judgment and can preserve property, hand it over.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians must not waste the estate or rush to use it before the orphan grows up; a rich guardian takes nothing, while a poor one may take a customary wage for work.
rows.anchor: حذر أن يبلغوا، فيلزمكم تسليم المال إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the orphans receive their property, take witnesses so the guardian can prove delivery if a dispute arises; God sufficiently reckons and recompenses.
rows.anchor: لكي إن وقع اختلاف أمكن الولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers deny resurrection, claiming worldly life is the only life.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says they recognize their Lord by necessity; another says they face His questioning and reproach, supported by their admission that resurrection is true, though too late to benefit them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وقفوا على مسألة ربهم وتوبيخه إياهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will admit that resurrection is true when it can no longer help them, then be told to taste punishment for their disbelief.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying the meeting with God lose when the Hour suddenly arrives; they lament neglecting the work of the Hereafter during worldly life.
rows.anchor: قصرنا وضيعنا عمل الآخرة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sins are burdens on their backs; on leaving the grave, their evil deed appears foul and reeking and says it will now ride them as they rode it in life.
rows.anchor: استقبله عمله أقبح شيء صورة، وأخبثه ريحا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people argued against his abandoning idols and threatened that they would harm him; he answers that God guided him to worship and oneness, and he fears only God’s will.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge encompasses everything completely; Abraham asks if they will take heed and abandon idols.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks why they fear idols but do not fear associating with God beings for whom they have no revealed proof, and whether monotheists or polytheists deserve security from punishment.
rows.anchor: ما ليس لكم في إشراكه بالله حجة وبرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do not mix faith with shirk are secure from punishment and guided to God’s religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s conclusive proof is scripture, messenger, and clarification; their unbelief occurs by God’s will, since He could have guided everyone had He willed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Bring your witnesses” means bring and summon them; the remainder is self-evident in the source.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s prohibitions begin with avoiding association and treating parents well, and forbid killing children from poverty, open or secret adultery, and killing except in lawful retaliation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protect orphans’ assets by improving and growing them; a needy guardian may take a customary amount, and the property is guarded until puberty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give full measure and fair weight without shortchanging or excess; requiring extra from the giver or too little from the recipient would exceed what each can bear.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When speaking or testifying, state the truth even when it concerns a close relative.
rows.anchor: إذا شهدتم أو تكلمتم فقولوا الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the religion of upright monotheism, the most upright religion; divergent paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and idol worship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divergent paths mislead from God’s religion; God commanded this in scripture so people would guard themselves from them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh accuses the magicians of conspiring with Moses in Egypt to seize it and expel its people through magic, then threatens them.
rows.anchor: فيما بينكم وبين موسى في مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crosswise cutting means severing one limb from each opposite side.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يقطع من كل شق طرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians say they return to their Lord in monotheism and sincerity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say Pharaoh resents them only because they believed in the signs Moses brought, the staff and the hand.
rows.anchor: ما أتى به موسى من العصا واليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They pray for patience under crucifixion and mutilation so they will not return to disbelief, and for death as Muslims following Moses’ religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s officials say Moses will corrupt the land by calling people to oppose Pharaoh and worship another; Pharaoh made small idols for the people and claimed lordship over them.
rows.anchor: كان قد صنع لقومه أصناما صغارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh resumes killing Israelite boys after stopping, leaves the girls for labor and service, and asserts his power; the Israelites complain to Moses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the deferral period of sacred months expires, fight polytheists wherever found, capture and besiege them, and lie in wait on every route.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they abandon shirk, establish obligatory prayer, and pay zakat from money, crops, and livestock, release them; God forgives those who repent and believe.
rows.anchor: إن الله غفور رحيم } لمن تاب وآمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If an enemy asks for protection, grant it so he can hear the Quran and receive God’s proof; then escort him to safety, even if he remains in shirk, so he can decide what to do.
rows.anchor: فاجعله في أمن { حتى يسمع كلام الله } القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are ignorant people who do not know God’s religion and oneness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day each person tests the recompense of the good or evil sent ahead; they return to God, true owner and just judge, while their fabrications vanish.
rows.anchor: جزاء ما قدمت من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain and grows plants, created hearing and sight, and brings believers from disbelievers, plants from earth, and people from semen, as well as their opposites.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs the affairs of this world and the next; since people admit He does these things, they should fear Him and associate nothing with Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God who does all this is the true Lord, unlike alleged partners; after God’s worship there is only misguidance, meaning Satan’s worship and beings unable to provide, give life, or cause death.
rows.anchor: ليس هؤلاء الذين جعلتم معه شركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s decree of wretchedness and abandonment is confirmed for those who persist in disbelief; they will not believe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of those who obstruct God’s way was explained earlier.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot escape God on earth; their punishment is delayed, not beyond His power, and they have no protectors. Their punishment is multiplied for misleading followers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could not hear because God prevented belief: they were deaf to truth, blind to it, and unable to find guidance.
rows.anchor: فكانوا صما عن الحق فلا يسمعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose themselves by ending in the Fire; their fabrications are gone and useless, and they are the greatest losers in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe, do good, and humble themselves before their Lord are at peace and settled; alternatively, they have repented.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss of humbling themselves before their Lord is that they repented.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s brothers say they raced to see who could run fastest, left him by their clothes, and claim a wolf ate him; they expect Jacob not to believe them because he suspects them in this story.
rows.anchor: نشتد ونعدو ليتبين أينا أسرع عدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blood on Joseph’s shirt was false: it was the blood of a young goat, not his own.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says their souls embellished another affair about Joseph; his beautiful patience contains no anguished complaint, and God is his aid in enduring their account.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي لا جزع فيه ولا شكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveling party sends its water-drawer to the well; Joseph clings to the bucket rope and is pulled up, prompting the man’s joyful announcement.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي يرد الماء ليستقي للقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water-drawer and merchants conceal Joseph as merchandise, claiming someone entrusted him as goods; God knows what they do to him.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: هذه بضاعة استبضعها بعض أهل الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s brothers call him their runaway slave and sell him for a low, forbidden price because he is free: twenty-two dirhams. They do not recognize his standing with God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s blessings are His favors, too numerous to count; the human being here means the disbeliever, who wrongs himself and denies his Lord’s favor.
rows.anchor: إنعام الله عليكم { لا تحصوها } لا تطيقوا عدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Keep me apart” means distance me and place me far away.
rows.anchor: بعدني واجعلني من على جانب بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols caused many people to go astray; whoever follows Abraham’s religion belongs to him, while God may forgive disobedience short of shirk.
rows.anchor: أي: ضلوا بسببها { فمن تبعني } على ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham settled Ishmael and his descendants in barren Mecca by the sacred House, which God had decreed would arise there, so they could establish prayer and worship.
rows.anchor: بواد غير ذي زرع } مكة حرسها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks that people’s hearts yearn to visit the House and that they receive fruits to affirm God’s oneness and glorify Him; the fruit request was discussed in al-Baqara.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disbelieved God’s signs of oneness, including the Quran, and meeting Him, meaning resurrection; their efforts are null, and God humiliates them in the Fire without regard.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses Muhammad and introduces the report and story of Moses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the way to Egypt, while his wife was in labor, Moses saw what looked like fire and told her to wait; he hoped to bring a flame or find a guide because he had lost the road.
rows.anchor: في طريقه إلى مصر لما أخذ امرأته الطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses approached, God called him; remove his sandals because they were untanned donkey hide, and he stood in the sacred, purified valley called Tuwā.
rows.anchor: من جلد حمار ميت غير مدبوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Moses for prophethood and told him to listen to the revelation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is commanded to establish prayer in order to remember God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not create the heavens and earth frivolously: He created them to reward His allies and punish His enemies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Amusement” means a woman, or alternatively a child; if God took one, it would be from Himself and hidden from people, but He does not do so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God casts the Quranic truth against the disbelievers’ falsehood, demolishing it until it vanishes; they face woe for attributing unworthy things to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All in the heavens and earth belong to God as servants and property; angels do not disdain worship, tire of it, or weaken in their night-and-day glorification.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged earthly gods are idols; the challenge asks whether they can bring the dead back to life.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give full measure and do not be among those who reduce people’s measure or weight.
rows.anchor: أوفوا الكيل } أتموه { ولا تكونوا من المخسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior passage explains Moses completing the term; a glowing coal is a piece and flame from a fire.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was called from the right bank of the valley, in the blessed patch where God spoke to him and granted prophethood, from beside the tree.
rows.anchor: بتكليم الله سبحانه فيها موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Taste what you did” means taste the punishment that is its consequence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My earth is vast” was revealed to encourage people in Mecca who could not practice their religion openly to migrate.
rows.anchor: لا يقدرون على إظهار دينهم على الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone dies wherever they live, so believers should not remain in the abode of shirk.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will settle the believers who do good in rooms of Paradise, meaning its palaces.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the hearts of those who do not know the proofs of monotheism, just as He sealed their hearts so they failed to understand.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad must be patient because God’s promise of victory and empowerment is true; doubting disbelievers must not unsettle him or make him abandon religion.
rows.anchor: في نصرك وتمكينك { حق ولا يستخفنك } لا يستفزنك عن دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pregnancy weakens a mother again and again, and weaning lasts two years because she nurses her child then; God commands gratitude to Him and the parents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if parents strive against the child, he should keep their company honorably; follow those who return to God, meaning Muhammad and his Companions. The verse was revealed about Saʿd b. Abi Waqqas.
rows.anchor: يعني: اسلك سبيل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Luqman’s story, his son asks how God knows a hidden sin; even mustard-seed-sized evil in a rock, heaven, or earth is brought forth for recompense, since God subtly extracts it and knows its location.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resolving to do what is right is among the obligatory matters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not turn away from people out of arrogance or walk swaggering and conceitedly.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walk moderately, neither proudly nor too quickly, lower the voice, and recognize the donkey’s braying as the ugliest sound.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected celestial bodies and earthly seas, rivers, and animals for people’s benefit; outward favors include beauty and stature, and inward favor is knowledge.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil calls people toward the causes of the blazing punishment, yet they follow him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Submitting one’s face means turning to God’s obedience; being good means being a monotheistic believer. Such a person holds the unbreakable, firmest handle; all matters return to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust is God’s prescribed obligations, whose fulfillment earns reward and betrayal punishment; God made the heavens, earth, and mountains understand and speak, but they declined from fear, not disobedience.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam accepted the trust, thereby wronging himself and being naïve about God’s command and the burden assumed.
rows.anchor: غرا بأمر الله سبحانه وما احتمل من الأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Betrayal through disobedience brings punishment to hypocrites and polytheists; God graciously accepts believers’ repentance and is forgiving and merciful.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disbeliever prays to God repentantly in hardship, then forgets Him and stops worshiping after receiving blessings; the command to enjoy disbelief briefly is a threat of the Fire.
rows.anchor: نسي الله الذي كان يتضرع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person obedient at night and wary of the Hereafter is not equal to a sinner; the learned and ignorant are likewise unequal, and people of understanding heed God’s reminders.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those excelling in this life are monotheists who obey God, and their reward is Paradise. They should migrate away from disbelievers; the patient receive reward without measure.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative particle in “good and evil are not equal” is redundant; answer evil with better: anger with patience, ignorance with forbearance, and injury with pardon, making an enemy a close friend.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those patient in restraining anger and enduring harm attain this trait; the great share is Paradise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan’s incitement turns someone from forbearance, seek God’s protection and continue to be forbearing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs of oneness; if disbelievers refuse prostration, the angels glorify and pray night and day without tiring.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One diverted from faith is someone turned away from good.
rows.anchor: يؤفك عنه } يصرف عن الإيمان به { من أفك } صرف عن الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “May the liars be killed” means the faction-making liars are cursed.
rows.anchor: قتل الخراصون } لعن الكذابون، يعني: المقتسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those immersed in heedlessness are distracted and careless.
rows.anchor: الذين هم في غمرة } غفلة { ساهون } لاهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers mockingly ask when Judgment Day is; punishment arrives when they burn in the Fire, and its keepers tell them to taste what they had rushed to demand.
rows.anchor: يسألون أيان يوم الدين } متى يوم الجزاء؟ استهزاء منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing are in gardens and springs, receiving their Lord’s reward; before entering, they excelled in good.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They used to sleep only a little during the night.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples of Mecca had no messenger come without calling him a sorcerer or madman.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Did they advise one another?” is a rebuke implying that some instructed others to disbelieve; rather, they are transgressors.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is blameless for turning away after conveying the message; he should remind people of God’s days, since reminders benefit believers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created jinn and humans to worship by commanding and inviting them; alternatively, the intended group is the believers among them, as in Ibn ʿAbbas’s reading.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no creature to provide or feed, since He is the Provider and feeder; “the Strong” means surpassing in strength.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The star/herb” is vegetation without a stalk that does not survive winter; plants and trees prostrate by submitting to God’s will.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the sky and established the balance of justice; people must not transgress its measure but weigh fairly without shortchanging.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is laid out for jinn and humans, bearing kinds of fruit, date-palm sheaths, grain leaves or straw, and provision in fragrant plants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are blessings for jinn and humans and signs of God’s oneness; the repeated question emphasizes and recalls His favors.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Inevitable” is the Resurrection because it surely comes and none can deny it; the question magnifies its affair, like asking “What is Zayd?”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud and ʿAd denied Resurrection. Thamud were destroyed by a cry exceeding its limit, and ʿAd by a fierce wind that defied its keepers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The slight-measurers deny people’s rights: they take their full measure but reduce what they measure or weigh for others.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be resurrected on the great Day when people rise from their graves before the Lord; certainty of resurrection would have stopped their cheating.
rows.anchor: من قبورهم { لرب العالمين } والمعنى أنهم لو أيقنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No indeed” rebukes them; sinners’ deeds are fixed in Sijjin, below seven earths and the abode of Iblis and his troops, beyond what the Prophet and his people knew.
rows.anchor: مكتوب مثبت عليهم في { سجين } في أسفل سبع أرضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what unbelievers conceal in their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is news of painful punishment, except for believers who do good: they receive reward that is not diminished or cut off.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The slanderer and backbiter gossips about and disparages others; the verse was revealed about Umayya b. Khalaf or, alternatively, al-Walid b. al-Mughira, who disparaged the Prophet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He amassed and prepared wealth for the future; alternatively, he counted it repeatedly in great quantity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He imagines wealth will keep him alive; the rebuke denies this, and he will be cast into al-Hutamah, the Fire.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting good things are better in outcome and are the best reward servants can hope to receive in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The level earth will have no buildings or trees; Ibn Mujahid reports from his father that it will have no covering or canopy.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: “We gathered them” means assembled; none was left behind, so all were present.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: People are presented in rows, meaning all gathered together.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said believers would constitute eighty of 120 rows on Judgment Day, amounting first to a third and then half of the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه ذات يوم:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet described prophets with few or no followers, then saw his own community fill the horizon and the passes around Mecca; seventy thousand enter Paradise without reckoning. He identified them as those who avoid ruqya, cautery, and omens and trust God; he prayed that ʿUkkasha be among them.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله: ما تقولون؟ فأخبروه، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Has the story reached you?” means the story of Moses has indeed reached Muhammad; al-Suddi gives the same gloss.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses saw what seemed to him fire, though it was actually light; “I saw a fire” means he saw a light, according to al-Suddi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hoped for a flame to warm his family, as another verse says, since it was winter; here he also hoped to find a guide to the road.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: “Guidance” means people who would show Moses the road.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: “Guidance” means someone to direct him along the road.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Moses was off the road, walking in reliance on his Lord without knowing the way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses reached it, he reached what he had thought was fire.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed people were reduced to harvested, lifeless remains.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: God did not create the Garden, Fire, death, resurrection, or reckoning as play.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The heavens and earth and what lies between them were not created in vain.

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Creation exists for resurrection and reckoning, and for the Garden and Fire.
rows.anchor: إنما خلقناهما للبعث والحساب، والجنة والنار.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: “Amusement” means a woman in the dialect of Yemen.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: “Amusement” means a consort and a child.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: “From Our presence” means from with Us.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: “If We were doing so” means that God would not do it; this rebuts the polytheists’ claim that angels are God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن المشركين قالوا: إن الملائكة بنات الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial that God has a child is linked to the statement that He has no consort, in 6:101.
rows.anchor: أنى يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth cast against falsehood is the Quran.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falsehood means the polytheists’ shirk; Qatada says the truth cast against it is God’s Book, and “demolishes” means defeats and vanishes.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The disbelievers face punishment for claiming that the angels are God’s daughters; this is their lie.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: مما تكذبون، لقولهم: إن الملائكة بنات الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings near God are angels, who do not become proud or weary of worship; Mujahid and Qatada gloss “not tire” as not exhausted.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The angels’ tireless glorification is like the effortless use of sight, hearing, and the self; none burdens a person.

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: People in Paradise will be inspired to praise and glorify God as naturally as breathing; another report attributes the same to Jabir.
rows.anchor: إن أهل الجنة يلهمون الحمد والتسبيح كما تلهمون النفس

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said the heavens creak, rightly, because no handspan lacks an angel prostrating or bowing; another report says each space has an angel standing, bowing, or prostrating.
rows.anchor: ليس فيها موضع شبر إلا وعليه ملك ساجد أو راكع

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: There is no handspan in the seven heavens without an angel standing, bowing, or prostrating.
rows.anchor: ليس في السموات السبع موضع شبر إلا وعليه ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the thicket denied the messengers; Shuʿayb was sent to two peoples, and the thicket is a grove.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Will you not fear God?” means “Will you not be wary of God?” and repeats the earlier exhortation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb calls himself trustworthy, commands fear and obedience, and says his reward is due only from the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: {إن أجري} [الشعراء: 127] إن جزائي، أي: إن ثوابي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving full measure means not reducing people’s rights; al-Suddi also says not to reduce measure or weight.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The upright qistas means justice; Mujahid says justice in the Roman language.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: According to Mujahid, qistas means justice in the Roman language.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not deprive people of what is theirs; the people of Shuʿayb habitually short-measured and short-weighed.
rows.anchor: وكانوا أصحاب تطفيف ونقص في الميزان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: “Do not go about the earth corrupting it” means do not travel around as corrupters; Hasan says not to be corrupters in the earth.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan’s gloss is that they must not be in the earth as corrupters.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: “I have fulfilled” means “I have completed,” and “there is no claim against me” means no way or cause against me.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: “God is guardian over what we say” means He is a witness; al-Suddi gives the same interpretation.
rows.anchor: تفسير مجاهد، وهو تفسير السدي: شهيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Moses completed the better and more generous of the two terms, the ten years.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قضى أوفاهما وأبرهما

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Moses completed the term he had agreed to fulfill.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Moses completed ten years, stayed ten more, and left after twenty years.
rows.anchor: قضى العشر السنين ثم أقام بعد ذلك عشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ṭur is the mountain.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Moses perceived what seemed to be fire, though it was actually light; it appeared to him as fire.
rows.anchor: أي: رأى نارا، وإنما كان نورا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Moses saw fire on the mountain while off the road and told his family to wait as he sought news of the road.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A glowing coal is the base of a tree; Moses hoped they could warm themselves because it was winter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses reached it, he came to what looked like fire to him.

rows.speaker: ابن مجاهد
rows.claim: The right bank of the valley was on Moses’ right.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Moses was called on the right side of the tree in the blessed patch; the verse’s word order is fronted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses fronting: Moses was called from the right bank of the valley, from beside the tree, within the blessed patch.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship God accompanies an order to migrate to Medina and later fight when commanded; the verse was revealed in Mecca before the migration.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Worship Me” means worship God in the land to which they were ordered to migrate, namely Medina.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone dies, as also stated in 23:15, 55:26, and 39:30; people return to God on Judgment Day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will settle believers who do good in Garden chambers with rivers beneath; they remain there forever, neither dying nor leaving.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How excellent the reward of the workers” means their excellent reward is Paradise.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet swore that one who sincerely testifies to God’s oneness and Muhammad’s messengerhood and stays upright enters Paradise; God promised seventy thousand of his community entry without reckoning or punishment, and he hoped his listeners and righteous families would dwell there.
rows.anchor: لا إله إلا الله صادقا من قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praised believers are those who are patient and rely on their Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How many” means “and how many.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they offer excuses, they cannot return to the world to make amends by believing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people every kind of Quranic example so they might remember; disbelievers asked the Prophet for a sign, then called him a liar when shown one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the hearts of those who meet Him while committing shirk.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should be patient because God truly promised victory over polytheists and the triumph of his religion; he must not be provoked or follow their call to abandon it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those lacking certainty are polytheists urging the Prophet to leave his religion.
rows.anchor: ما يدعونك إليه من ترك دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is for God’s blessing; the believer who is grateful benefits himself, while the ungrateful rejects the blessing. God is independent of creation and deserves praise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman warns his son against shirk because it wrongs and harms the person who commits it; Hasan says it diminishes oneself, and al-Suddi calls it a great sin.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: When 6:82 said believers had not mixed faith with injustice, the Companions asked who was free of injustice; 31:13 was revealed to identify shirk as the injustice meant.
rows.anchor: وأينا لم يظلم؟ فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes three wrongs: shirk is unforgiven, sins between a servant and God may be forgiven, and wrongs between people are not left without reciprocal redress.
rows.anchor: الظلم ثلاثة: فظلم لا يغفره الله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: “We enjoined the human being concerning his parents” means enjoining kindness to them.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: “Weakness upon weakness” describes the mother’s repeated weakness; Ibn Mujahid, Mujahid, and Qatada offer related glosses of the child’s burden, weakness, or effort.
rows.anchor: ضعفا على ضعف، في تفسير الحسن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Separation” means weaning; a Prophetic report says there is no nursing after weaning, and Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas did not count nursing after two years.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “To Me is the destination” means the Resurrection; reports say God’s pleasure and anger correspond to a parent’s pleasure and anger and describe Paradise or Hell’s gates for one pleasing or angering parents, even if wronged.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says good deeds have ever higher forms, culminating in giving one’s life for God, while worse sins culminate in disobeying one’s parents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the rock is the one on which the whale rests and which supports the earths.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman warns that God will account for a mustard-seed-sized deed wherever found, and knows its location; He is subtle in bringing it forth and knowledgeable of its place.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Prayer and commanding right mean calling to monotheism; forbidding wrong means forbidding shirk. Abu al-ʿAliya similarly says commanding God’s worship and forbidding idols fulfills the command.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resolved matters include patience through affliction; the source glosses resolve as decisively cutting something off.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to God and His Messenger brings great success: escape from Hell to Paradise.
rows.anchor: النجاة العظيمة من النار إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The trust offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains comprised reward and punishment, obedience and disobedience.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says worship was offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains with its rewards and punishments; they refused it, while Adam accepted.
rows.anchor: عرض العبادة على السموات، والأرض، والجبال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the human’s trust as prayer, fasting, and washing after major impurity.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God entrusted Adam with prayer, fasting, and washing after major impurity; keeping them makes one God’s servant, neglecting them His enemy, and one could falsely claim to have done them.
rows.anchor: ثلاث من حفظهن فهو عبدي حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam, the human bearer, was unjust to himself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ignorant” means ignorant of his Lord, describing the polytheist.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the hypocrite and polytheist wronged and betrayed the trust; God punishes them and forgives believers who repent from shirk, admitting them to Paradise through mercy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is merciful to believers and admits them to Paradise through that mercy.
